scenario: btrfs subvolume mount at /home whose single listed uuid has the qgroups directory present (initialized) but qgroups_enabled false and qgroups_mode null

fixture.mountinfo:
25 30 0:30 / / rw,relatime shared:1 - btrfs /dev/mapper/root rw,space_cache,subvolid=257,subvol=/
26 25 0:30 /@home /home rw,relatime shared:1 - btrfs /dev/mapper/root rw,space_cache,subvolid=256,subvol=/@home
27 25 0:31 / /proc rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime shared:5 - proc proc rw
28 25 0:32 / /sys rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime shared:6 - sysfs sysfs rw
29 25 0:33 / /tmp rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime shared:8 - xfs /dev/mapper/data rw,attr2,inode64,noquota

rationale: preseal-amendment.md §C2 final rules (btrfs bullet) plus the kernel sources: mount resolution (amendment, 'Mount resolution' bullet): the fixture mountinfo is parsed per proc.rst §3.5 field layout [S082]; candidate covering mountpoints for realpath /home/quota/disabled are '/' and '/home'; the longest component-prefix wins and neither covering mountpoint occurs more than once in the file, so the ambiguous_overmount refusal does not apply, and the trailing empty line is ignored. The chosen line '26 25 0:30 /@home /home rw,relatime shared:1 - btrfs /dev/mapper/root rw,space_cache,subvolid=256,subvol=/@home' is parsed by its separator and its last three fields, giving fstype 'btrfs', source '/dev/mapper/root' and super options 'rw,space_cache,subvolid=256,subvol=/@home'; no backslash escapes occur, so no escape rejection. Device gate (amendment, 'Device mismatch PREEMPTS the filesystem table' bullet): the chosen fstype is btrfs and the path's stat major is 0 (st_dev 0:57, the anonymous btrfs subvolume device, S081 = fs/btrfs/inode.c, inode.c:8246 'stat->dev = BTRFS_I(inode)->root->anon_dev'), so the btrfs equality skip applies and the mismatch against the mount major:minor 0:30 does not preempt the filesystem table; a nonzero btrfs stat major mismatching the mount would instead give unknown/n/a/device_mismatch. Device-to-uuid resolution (amendment, 'Fixture source resolution'): the raw decoded source '/dev/mapper/root' is looked up in device_links and yields the mapped basename 'dm-0', which is compared against the uuid records' devices lists; exactly one record lists 'dm-0', so the zero/multiple-match refusal does not apply. Quota classification (amendment, btrfs bullet): the qgroups directory is present (qgroups true, i.e. initialized) but qgroups_enabled is false, so the amendment's row 'Present plus enabled=false -> disabled/n/a/btrfs_qgroups_disabled' applies, giving quota_state 'disabled', enforcement 'n/a', basis 'btrfs_qgroups_disabled'; presence of the directory alone would have meant only 'initialized', which is why the enabled attribute is now required [S079 = fs/btrfs/sysfs.c, qgroup_enabled_show reports the BTRFS_QGROUP_STATUS_FLAG_ON bit as an exact 0/1]. qgroups_mode is null because real mode reads qgroups/enabled first and reads mode only when enabled is 1, which is not the case here; the kernel's mode reader is additionally guarded by ASSERT(btrfs_qgroup_enabled(fs_info)) [S079, qgroup_mode_show], so mode must not be consulted for a disabled qgroups state. The directory's existence is the initialization artifact of btrfs_sysfs_add_qgroups, created when qgroup support is first brought up and removed by btrfs_sysfs_del_qgroups [S080 = fs/btrfs/qgroup.c, call sites qgroup.c:441 and :1032 for add, :620, :689 and :1295 for delete], so directory presence and enabled state are distinct facts. Verdict (amendment, output/verdict section; precedence unchanged): the single path is disabled with no enabled and no unknown sibling, so exit 0 and finding_id 'QUOTA_DISABLED'; per the amendment's boundary text QUOTA_DISABLED is not a capacity or health verdict. Fixture-format conformance (amendment, 'Paths', UUID and record rules): the path is nonempty, unique, normalized and absolute with no dot/dotdot components, st_dev '0:57' is canonical decimal MAJ:MIN, the UUID key is canonical, the device basename 'dm-0' is a plain nonempty basename, and the uuid record carries exactly the keys devices, qgroups, qgroups_enabled, qgroups_mode with bool / bool-or-null / mode-or-null types. The btrfs super options carry no quota key, so quota_option_keys is empty by the amendment's btrfs rule.
